**Cahaya Seri Catering Sdn. Bhd. – Supplier Vetting Snapshot** | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Registration** | SYN‑000286; Private Ltd.; incorporated 20 Nov 2017; active; based in Sabah. | | **Business** | Wholesale distributor of frozen food to restaurants (Food & Beverage). | | **Ownership & Management** | • Directors: Managing Director, Executive Director, Independent Director (appointed 2024).
• Shareholders: Director 1 (≈ 99 %) and Director 2 (≈ 1 %). | | **Financial Highlights** (FY 2024 vs FY 2022) | • Revenue: **RM 4.42 M** (↑ 5 %).
• Net profit: **RM 179 k** (↑ 3 %).
• Gross margin: **≈ 50 %**; Operating margin: **≈ 8 %**.
• EBITDA: **RM 496 k** (EBITDA margin ≈ 11 %).
• Total assets: **RM 4.77 M**; Equity: **RM 1.95 M** (Equity ≈ 41 %).
• Leverage: **Debt‑to‑Equity ≈ 1.45**; Interest coverage ≈ 3×. | | **Liquidity** | Quick ratio **1.4** (good); cash‑to‑revenue **≈ 7 %**; cash balance **RM 305 k** (down from RM 352 k). | | **Cash Flow** | Operating cash flow **RM 220 k** (down from RM 434 k); free cash flow **‑RM 20 k** (negative in 2024). | | **Operational Efficiency** | Cash conversion cycle ~ 137 days (improved); inventory turnover ↑ to **4.13×**; receivables turnover **4.55×**. | | **Audit** | Audited by “Audit Firm 8”; unqualified opinions for both years. | | **Litigation (as of 2024)** | 6 cases where the company is the defendant:
• 2 settled (construction, employment).
• 1 judgment entered (debt recovery, claim RM 97.6 k).
• 2 pending (winding‑up petition RM 355.9 k; tenancy dispute RM 110.6 k).
• 1 dismissed (tenancy, RM 28.4 k). | | **Key Risks / Considerations** | • High concentration of ownership (≈ 99 % held by one director).
• Modest profitability and thin net margin (≈ 4 %).
• Declining operating cash flow and negative free cash flow in 2024.
• Ongoing legal exposure, including a pending winding‑up petition. | | **Overall Assessment** | A small, active frozen‑food wholesaler with stable revenues and solid gross margins, but limited profitability, cash‑flow pressure, and several legal disputes that merit further due‑diligence before onboarding as a supplier. |
